clue.text: At first, performance by hybrid yacht is variable

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it
a hybrid is a cross-bred mix, so the word it describes gets its letters mixed up

blocks.note: the opening letter of performance
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A review says a hybrid-powered yacht performs unevenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchy is uneven in quality, good in places and poor in others, so it varies.

clue.text: Correct point at end of summary

indicators.note: at the end of means placed after, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: a precis is a short summary
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An editor makes a correction to the last point of a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct as an adjective means accurate and exact, which is what precise means.

clue.text: Either way, note clear doctrine

indicators.note: either way means read forwards or backwards, the result being identical

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to clear a sum as profit is to net it

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, the teaching is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true by a group, a synonym for doctrine.

clue.text: Con man and cattle thief head off after horse

indicators.note: head off means remove the top, so the first letter of the word goes
after means placed following, so this piece comes behind the other

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for horse
a rustler steals livestock

explanation.surface: A swindler and a livestock thief ride off after a horse, Wild West style.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is someone who cons people out of money, a swindler or fraudster.

clue.text: Saving a pound on fine carpet

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after what follows it in the clue

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a rug is a small carpet
taken as written
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A thrifty shopper saves a pound on a good carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving as an adjective describes someone careful with money, which is exactly what thrifty or economical means.

clue.text: Comments on targets

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
marks are targets, as in an easy mark

explanation.surface: Someone gives feedback on goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks are things said or written as observations, so they are synonyms of comments.

clue.text: Biscuit needs drink — get urn working!

indicators.note: working means in operation or in motion, so the letters are churned into new order

blocks.note: gin is a spirit
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants a cuppa with their biscuit, so they urge the tea urn to be switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginger nut is a hard ginger-flavoured British biscuit, popular for dunking in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a crunchy round cookie flavoured with spice, one specific example of a biscuit.

clue.text: Coat for one said to be in need?

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the description

blocks.clueFragment: one said to be in need
blocks.note: one who is in need is someone who lacks things

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to wear when said to be hard up, as if picking an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that lacker, one who lacks, is an invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a glossy varnish applied as a protective layer, so it is a coat of finish.

clue.text: Plump for Conservative partner

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
hubby is an informal word for husband

explanation.surface: A voter decides to choose the Conservative partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby describes someone pleasantly fat or rounded, a close synonym of plump.

clue.text: Comic character in the end's beaten danger

indicators.note: beaten as in whisked or battered: the preceding words are knocked into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a menace is a threat or danger

explanation.surface: A comic-book character is finally defeated, along with whatever danger he posed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis the Menace is the long-running mischievous boy of the British comic The Beano.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the famous troublemaking star of a children's comic, so he is literally a comic character.

clue.text: Many try to turn back shooter

indicators.note: turning back means going the other way, so the letters read from right to left

blocks.note: a lot means many
to sip a drink is to try or taste it

explanation.surface: Lots of people attempt something and then give up and head home.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooter is slang for a gun, and a pistol is a small handgun.

clue.text: Sharp comment's signal to pursue end of office party outside

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the following word
to pursue is to come behind, so that piece is placed after the next one

blocks.note: a barb is a cutting remark
the final letter of office
a cue is a signal to act or speak

explanation.surface: Someone's pointed remark becomes the cue to chase the end of the office party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office party' looks like a phrase, but office supplies one letter and party belongs with outside as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is a social gathering held in the open air with food grilled over a fire.

clue.text: Do without alcohol?

blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to give up drinking
setter's reading: a do is a social event, and one with no alcohol serves only a hot non-alcoholic drink

explanation.walkthrough: Do reads as a verb telling you to abstain, but it is the noun meaning a party or function.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where guests are served cups of a hot brewed drink and cakes rather than wine or beer is a dry social occasion.

clue.text: Put off job organising open day

indicators.note: organising means putting in order, so the following letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: a post is a job
taken as written, then rearranged
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone delays the task of arranging an open day.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off an event is to delay it until later, which is to postpone it.

clue.text: Guard posted by railway

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece sits directly next to the other

blocks.note: a letter posted is sent
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A guard is stationed beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier stationed to keep watch, a synonym for a guard on duty.

clue.text: Journalist's piece covering cheap accommodation

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: a bit is a piece
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A reporter writes an article on low-cost housing.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British term for a single rented room used for both living and sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room rented flat is among the cheapest forms of housing, so it is budget lodging.

clue.text: Mimic bird, teal maybe?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word could be something else, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an emu is a large flightless Australian bird
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird imitates another, perhaps a teal duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teal maybe' looks like a bird defined by example, since a teal is a duck, but teal is the jumbled fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to copy or imitate them, so it is a verb synonym of mimic.

clue.text: Queen follows attendants in coach

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a train is a retinue of attendants
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen travels behind her retinue in a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is someone who instructs athletes or teams, which is what a coach does.

clue.text: Drive past public area with king cheered heartily

indicators.note: heartily is read as at the heart, so only the central letter is kept
with means alongside, so the pieces are simply joined together

blocks.note: something overt is open and public
A is the abbreviation for area
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the middle letter of cheered

explanation.surface: A king is cheered heartily as he is driven past the crowd in a public square.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake is to catch up with and pass another vehicle on the road.

clue.text: Nothing felt different about America recently

indicators.note: different means changed, so the preceding word's letters are altered in order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written, then rearranged
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Recently, people have felt nothing has changed in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom meaning lately or in the recent past.

clue.text: Investigate when chopper's sent up with explosive device

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means sent upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
with means together alongside, so the next piece joins on

blocks.note: an axe is a tool for chopping
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: Detectives look into a case where a helicopter was blown up by a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper suggests a helicopter alongside explosive, but here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or scrutinise it closely, a synonym of investigate.

clue.text: Gutting easier, after bottom of boat secured new cushion

indicators.note: gutting means removing the insides, so only the outer letters survive
secured means held fast around, so the first piece encloses the next
after means placed later, so this piece follows the others

blocks.note: the keel runs along the bottom of a boat
N is the abbreviation for new
the first and last letters of easier

explanation.surface: Cleaning a fish is easier once a fresh cushion is secured in the bottom of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneeler is a padded cushion for kneeling on, typically in church pews.

clue.text: Fail to turn up for trial, where posh politician's boy is put in prison

definitions.text: Fail to turn up for trial

indicators.note: something put in is placed inside, so these pieces go within the next

blocks.note: a jail is a prison
U means upper-class
MP is a Member of Parliament
B is a dictionary abbreviation for boy

explanation.surface: A smart politician's son ends up behind bars after skipping his court date.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone released on bail who absconds rather than appearing in court has broken the bail terms, the idiom for absconding.

clue.text: Answer article describing unknown meadow flower

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around, so the outer pieces go around the next

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a is the indefinite article
Z is an algebraic unknown
a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

explanation.surface: An article answers a question by describing a mysterious meadow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An azalea is a flowering shrub related to the rhododendron, so it gives a flower.

clue.text: Invalidate points, blocking gold medal finally

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the middle of something, so these letters go inside
finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
N, north, is a compass point, here taken twice
the final letter of medal

explanation.surface: Judges cancel a competitor's points, denying them a gold medal at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul something is to declare it void or cancelled officially, so it is made invalid.

clue.text: Danger sign with repeated awful rain over night regularly cutting off end of glen

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the word it qualifies comes out jumbled
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
over here means spread above and around, so the repeated word wraps the next piece
cutting off the end means the last letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the word rain used twice, each time jumbled
the first, third and fifth letters of night
taken as written before its final letter is removed

explanation.surface: Driving through a glen at night in heavy rain, you see a sign warning of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: With gives W at the start, but in the surface it seems only to join the definition to the rest. The two jumbled RAINs sit either side of NGT.
explanation.definitionFit: A red reflective triangle placed behind a broken-down car on the road alerts other drivers to a hazard.

clue.text: Stick close by river

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces are set next to each other

blocks.note: the close of something is its end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay close beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out is to put up with something unpleasant, as in to tolerate or bear it.

clue.text: Church meeting briefly reviewed space below ground level

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is lopped off
reviewed is read as viewed again backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A church gathering is summarised and reassessed in an underground hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a room built beneath a house, often used for storage, so it lies underground.
